Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. # Promptly Done: Tacto Negotiation Arena (EHL Grand Finale 2026)

AI buyer agent for the [Tacto Negotiation Arena](https://arena.tacto.ai/).
The official kit is vendored in `negotiation-arena-kit/`.

## Run

```bash
cd negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit
cp .env.example .env   # ARENA_API_KEY, LLM_PROVIDER=openai, LLM_MODEL, LLM_API_KEY
uv sync --all-extras
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm
```

## Team tools (`negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/team/`)

Run from `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit`:

```bash
uv run python -m team.levers case:P01 --price 135.10        # what each lever is worth in EUR (no session used)
uv run python -m team.evaluate --sim --agent llm             # local simulator: free
uv run python -m team.evaluate --agent llm --label my-change # all hosted practice cases (10 sessions, asks first)
```

`team.evaluate` writes `runs/<time>_<label>/summary.md`: score per case vs. the previous run, the levers
left on the table and the supplier's reasons. Our practice quota is 200 sessions per day for the whole team.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
Mostly yes. The arithmetic is right, but three things in the email are off. This one came from the **dual** agent's opening message in the P01 run I just did.

## 1. The weighted cost argument: correct by the supplier's own figures
Brandlhuber said labour (LCI-C) rose 2.7 % and is 30 % of their cost, and steel (PPI-C241) rose 6.5 % and is 24 % of their cost:

| Driver | Change | × Share | = Effect on price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Labour (LCI-C) | +2.7 % | 30 % | +0.81 % |
| Steel (PPI-C241) | +6.5 % | 24 % | +1.56 % |
| **Total** | | | **+2.37 % ≈ 2.4 %** |

The ask is 138.55 / 126.53 − 1 = **+9.5 %**, so their own figures explain about 7.1 points less. The changes match the data package: LCI-C 116.5 → 119.6 = +2.66 %, PPI-C241 99.4 → 105.9 = +6.54 %.

## 2. The electricity line: true, but weak
PPI-D351 went 137.0 → 131.9 = **−3.7 %**, so that's correct. But the supplier never claimed electricity as a cost. In our own cost model (`cost_drivers.csv`) it's only 6 % of the part's cost, so it's worth −3.7 % × 6 % = **−0.22 %**. On our own weights the total is 0.32 × 2.66 + 0.26 × 6.54 + 0.06 × (−3.72) = **+2.33 %**, about the same as the email's figure.

The opening line ("electricity movements and the weighted arithmetic") is LLM filler.

## 3. The payment terms: the logic holds, the wording is wrong
At our 8 % interest rate, paying 30 days earlier costs us 125.39 × 0.08 × 30/365 = **€0.82/unit**. Option A is €1.13 cheaper, so it comes out about **€0.31/unit (~€2.4k/yr) better for us**. The kit's cost function confirms it:

| Option | Price cost | Payment-term cost | Freight | **C** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: 125.39, 30 days | 1,021,928 | +6,813 | 15,485 | **1,044,226** |
| B: 126.52, 60 days | 1,031,138 | 0 | 15,485 | **1,046,623** |

These figures leave out the margin-squeeze charge for this case (the case goal is "stabilise"), so they're slightly low.

**The problems are in how it's worded:**
- **Brandlhuber never asked for 30 days.** Their first mail had no payment terms at all. The "ask" was filled in from their current contract, `ctr:4600070110`, which already pays at 30 days ([strategy.py:280](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/strategy.py:280)). "You asked for payment 30 days net" puts words in their mouth. It is also backwards: 30 days is the status quo, so Option B asks *them* to give something.
- **The point is made twice.** "We gladly accept your requested shorter payment terms…" (written by the LLM) and "You asked for payment 30 days net: we can agree…" (written by code, [dual.py:772](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/dual.py:772)) say the same thing. Both claim an ask the supplier never made.

## 4. The opening price
Both options sit below today's price of €126.53, right after we conceded that +2.4 % is justified. A reader would expect roughly 126.53 × 1.024 ≈ **€129.5**. Our own should-cost for this part is **€132.64 before any margin**, and the negotiation history says Brandlhuber has "accepted below full cost to keep the volume" for 4 years. As an opening offer this is defensible. But it contradicts the email's own arithmetic and the "healthy, reliable partner" line, and in a stabilise case squeezing the supplier's margin adds to C. The deal still closed at 134.00 for a score of 0.765, so it didn't backfire here.

**Fixes I'd suggest:**
1. Only say "you asked for" when the payment terms came from the supplier's own term sheet or e-mail, not from their contract.
2. Stop the LLM from repeating the sentence code already writes.
3. Consider opening at about current price × (1 + the weighted effect) so the price is consistent with the argument.

Want me to make any of these changes?

> Dear customer,
> 
> Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.
> 
> For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.
> 
> To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.
> 
> We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.
> 
> Mit freundlichen Grüßen
> Franz Seidl
> Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH
> Dear Franz Seidl,
> 
> Thank you for your quote and for explaining the cost increases behind it. We recognise the pressure from rising alloy, labour and processing costs, but seek a lower fixed price in exchange for the terms offered below.
> 
> We are happy to accept your requested payment and agreement terms in Option A, with that concession reflected in its lower price. Option B retains our standard terms and gives you a longer customer commitment. Our standard payment term is 60 days net: paying earlier ties up our working capital, so an option with faster payment carries a lower price. You asked for payment 30 days net, 12.0-month agreement: we can agree to that - Option A grants it, and its price reflects what it is worth to you; Option B keeps our standard terms.
> 
> We can offer either of these packages - please choose the one that suits you better:
> Option A: EUR 4.39 per unit, fixed price, no index clause, payment 30 days net, 12.0-month agreement.
> Option B: EUR 5.36 per unit, fixed price, no index clause, payment 60 days net, 24-month agreement.
> 
> Could you share a cost breakdown for this part — material, conversion and overhead?
> 
> We would be pleased to agree a price basis that continues our relationship with Werdenfels.
> 
> Kind regards
> Purchasing
> Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH
> Dear customer,
> 
> Your offer is far below any calculation we can make. Please explain its basis. We value our cooperation and have made a step towards you. 
> 
> Our current Angebot stands at a price of €6.10 per unit, Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, no Preisgleitklausel. Material accounts for about 45 % of our cost; more detail we do not share. 
> 
> This offer stays valid for 30 days.
> 
> Mit freundlichen Grüßen
> Franz Seidl
> Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH
> Dear Franz Seidl,
> 
> We understand that our offer is below your calculation, recognise that material is only part of your costs, and thank you for moving towards us. We are holding our last offer because it prices the payment and commitment terms below, rather than relying on an assumed cost breakdown.
> 
> We are happy to accept your requested payment timing and agreement length in Option A, with faster payment reflected in its lower fixed price. Option B keeps our standard payment terms and offers a longer customer commitment, although it does not add a volume commitment. We keep our offer as it stands.
> 
> We can offer either of these packages - please choose the one that suits you better:
> Option A: EUR 4.39 per unit, fixed price, no index clause, payment 30 days net, 12.0-month agreement.
> Option B: EUR 5.36 per unit, fixed price, no index clause, payment 60 days net, 24-month agreement.
> 
> We hope this makes the basis of our offer clear and helps us reach an agreement.
> 
> Kind regards
> Purchasing
> Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH
> Dear customer,
> 
> Thank you for your ongoing partnership with Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH. We always strive to support your operations with our extensive inventory and reliable service. 
> 
> Regarding your latest proposal, we must candidly state that your offer is far below any calculation we can make. We have evaluated our possibilities thoroughly to support your needs while maintaining the quality you expect from us. 
> 
> This is our final offer (letztes Angebot). Please decide based on these terms: we can present a price of €6.10 per unit, a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this proposal remains valid for 7 days.
> 
> We hope this arrangement works for you and look forward to continuing our cooperation.
> 
> Mit freundlichen Grüßen
> Franz Seidl
> Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

content.text:
All 9 cases ran with the dual agent, and the practice quota went down by exactly 9 (413 → 404). Every case closed a deal. With P01 from earlier, the full dual run averages **57.0**, about level with v9's 56.9 (our best full run so far). That's one run per case, so it's within the usual noise.

| Case | Type | Price | Score | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | price_increase | 134.00 | 0.765 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/7d6bf0d94ccec665) |
| P02 | price_increase (copper) | 371.88 | 0.507 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/136d81f9aa6fc78b) |
| P03 | renewal | 433.08 | **0.900** | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/ab084a52bef41781) |
| P04 | renewal | 4.94 | 0.860 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/b7e45d9beaf6f90a) |
| P05 | rfq | 31.20 | 0.501 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/264c0139bee3530b) |
| P07 | bundling | 5.46 | 0.715 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/b02701d8a2831ff1) |
| P08 | raw_material | 5.47 | 0.242 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/48b48c9973cb49a1) |
| P10 | capacity | 31.60 | 0.671 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/8c5f67ba8ed119dc) |
| P11 | quality | 46.00 | 0.536 | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/85f06a8b3bba392f) |
| P18 | raw_material | 6.10 | **0.000** | [replay](https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/0f6dbf0a6e1ddbb7) |

The 9 new cases alone average 0.548. P18 and P08 are still the weakest, as before.

**P18 scored 0 because we took the supplier's opening offer unchanged.** Werdenfels opened at €6.10:
1. We offered €4.39 or €5.36, which is 28 % below their price.
2. They replied "far below any calculation we can make" and held at €6.10.
3. We sent **the exact same two options again** with "We keep our offer as it stands."
4. They made €6.10 their final offer and we accepted it.

That anchor was too low to be believable. Holding it when the supplier wouldn't move meant they never had a reason to come down, so we spent our rounds without gaining anything. P18 needs a more credible opening and a real concession path before the final offer.

The false "You asked for payment 30 days net, 12.0-month agreement" line from P01 shows up in P18 too. The supplier only quoted those as its standard terms. It's the same code path, so the fix I suggested for P01 covers both.

Everything is in C, the case's total cost (`cost.total_cost`), with our estimate of the supplier so
that strategic and bottleneck cases price a squeezed supplier too. Each round has a target C:

  anchor     the C of an opening price taken from the data: the lowest of the goal's cut off their
             quote, no increase at all (price increases), the best rival quote and a fair price
             (the supplier's should-cost plus a margin for the goal) - never deeper than
             MAX_ANCHOR_CUT, never below its cost floor or the price at which C stops falling.
             It is priced on OUR reference terms (payment days, volume, contract length): what the
             supplier asks beyond them is never absorbed into the target for free
  concession target = anchor + f(round) × (their C now − anchor), f rising and flattening, so the
             steps shrink - and a supplier that did not move gets half a step
  sheets     up to three term sheets that all cost us that target C: their terms at a lower price,
             a trade the supplier may value (e.g. faster payment) at a lower price still, and our
             preferred terms at a higher price. Which one it answers tells us what it values.
             When the supplier asked for a term (e.g. payment in 15 days): two sheets instead - yes
             to its ask at a lower price that still leaves it better off, or our terms at the target.

DECOY_GAP = 0.02  # the lean option: the recommended one 2 % cheaper and one term worse for the supplier
RECIPROCITY = 0.5  # our step answers theirs with at most this share of it
# A term we give the supplier is worth something to it (faster payment: its cost of money, more when
# short of cash) and costs us something (our interest). Between the two lies a gain for both sides;
# the sheet that gives the term splits it, so the supplier is better off taking it and so are we.
SURPLUS_SHARE = 0.5  # our share of that gain
ROUND_HORIZON = 6  # rounds per thread we plan for: the Live Final's cap leaves about this many
# The opening comes from the data. A fair price is the supplier's should-cost plus a margin the goal
# allows (relationship goals: the case's sustainable margin - below it C rises again).
FAIR_MARGIN = {"leverage": 0.05, "routine": 0.06, "quality_first": 0.08}
MAX_ANCHOR_CUT = 0.25  # never open more than 25 % under their price: below that it is not credible
CASH_SHORT_PREMIUM = 0.06  # a supplier short of cash values money this much more per year than we do
# Fields with a buyer reference (the plan): what the supplier asks beyond it is a give from us.
REFERENCE_FIELDS = ("payment_days", "volume_per_year", "contract_months", "lead_time_days", "index_clause")


    return round(est.point / (1 - margin), 2)  # margin on the price, as the arena counts it

    the anchor never goes below the price at which C stops falling."""

def ask_sheets(case, std, est, base, their_price, target, asks, lo, hi):
    """Two sheets when the supplier asked for something: [their ask, our reference].
    their ask   exactly what it asked for (e.g. payment in 15 days), at a lower price: between what
                the ask costs us (equal C) and what it is worth to the supplier (`give_price`), so
                taking it leaves both sides better off than the reference

        return []
    p = give_price(price_at(case, give, std, est, target, lo, hi), indifference_price(case, give, ref, p_ref, std, est))
    if p is None:

    p = max(p, lo)

            out.append((label, t))

    effect). Safe by construction: if the supplier takes the lean option, that is better for us."""

        if (v := step(case, f, lean[f], std, toward_supplier=False)) is not None:
            lean[f] = v

    if lean["unit_price"] < floor or lean in [t for _, t in out] or not must_haves_ok(case, lean, std):
        return out
    rest = [(label, t) for label, t in out if t is not middle][:1]
    return [("lean", lean), ("recommended", middle), *rest]

    so the recommended option in the middle looks like the sensible choice (decoy and compromise

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, play, strategy, writing
from arena_kit import claims as cl
from arena_kit.agents import BuyerAgent
from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok, total_cost
from arena_kit.sim import load_cases

PACKAGE = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "data" / "package"
CASES = load_cases()


def test_index_claims_are_the_arenas_arithmetic():
    case = CASES["case:S01"]  # its facts carry PPI-C2431 for 2025-08 and 2026-08
    got = cl.index_change(None, case, "PPI-C2431")
    assert got == (round((129.1 / 115.0 - 1) * 100, 1), "idx:PPI-C2431@2025-08", "idx:PPI-C2431@2026-08")
    claims = cl.candidates(None, case, "sup:70270", their_price=17.5)
    index = next(c for c in claims if c.key == "index:PPI-C2431")
    assert "+12.3%" in index.sentence and not index.favourable  # a rise argues the supplier's side


def test_a_claim_counts_once_per_case_a_rival_quote_once_per_supplier():
    ledger = cl.Ledger()
    idx = cl.Claim("index:X", "index", ["idx:X@2025-08", "idx:X@2026-08"], "")
    rival = cl.Claim("rival:offer:A", "rival", ["offer:A-1"], "")
    ledger.use(idx, "sup:A")
    ledger.use(rival, "sup:B")
    assert ledger.spent(idx, "sup:C") and ledger.spent(rival, "sup:B") and not ledger.spent(rival, "sup:C")


@pytest.mark.skipif(not (PACKAGE / "facts.json").is_file(), reason="needs the data package (arena data)")
def test_claims_from_the_package_match_facts_json():
    from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

    pkg = DataPackage(PACKAGE)
    facts = json.loads((PACKAGE / "facts.json").read_text())
    case = {
        "case_id": "case:X", "type": "price_increase", "trigger_doc": "doc:20260911-70110-P01",
        "parts": ["part:310010"], "suppliers": ["sup:70110"], "term_options": {},
        "refs": ["doc:20260911-70110-P01", "ctr:4600070110", "sc:70110@2026Q3"], "buyer": {},
    }  # fmt: skip
    out = {c.key: c for c in cl.candidates(pkg, case, "sup:70110", their_price=138.55)}
    assert out["notice"].figure == facts["doc:20260911-70110-P01"]["days"] == 51
    a, b = out["index:PPI-D351"].ids
    assert out["index:PPI-D351"].figure == round((facts[b]["value"] / facts[a]["value"] - 1) * 100, 1) == -3.7
    assert out["scorecard"].figure == facts["sc:70110@2026Q3"]["otd_pct"]
    assert not out["should_cost"].favourable  # 132.64 leaves no room under 138.55 - citing it would backfire
    assert max(out.values(), key=lambda c: c.strength).key == "notice"


def test_sheets_are_small_medium_large_around_the_target():
    """Lean / recommended / other: the recommended option costs the target; the lean one is it a bit
    cheaper with a term worse for the supplier, so it is even better for us if taken."""
    case = CASES["case:S02"]
    std = {"payment_days": 30, "lead_time_days": 35, "incoterm": "DAP"}
    their = {"unit_price": 20.0, "payment_days": 30, "lead_time_days": 35}
    est = strategy.Estimate(None)
    target = total_cost(case, {**their, "unit_price": 18.5}, std)
    out = strategy.sheets(case, std, est, their, target, ["payment_days"], floor=10)
    assert [label for label, _ in out][:2] == ["lean", "recommended"] and len(out) == 3
    lean, middle = out[0][1], out[1][1]
    assert abs(total_cost(case, middle, std) - target) / target < 0.001
    assert lean["unit_price"] == round(middle["unit_price"] * (1 - strategy.DECOY_GAP), 2)
    assert lean["payment_days"] > middle["payment_days"]  # the term the supplier values, moved our way
    assert total_cost(case, lean, std) < total_cost(case, middle, std)

content.text:
No option we send can now go more than **25 % below the supplier's current price**. All tests pass (81 passed, 1 skipped). I haven't committed it or run it against the live arena yet.

**What the fix was.** For P01 I suggested three fixes, none of them implemented:
1. **Stop the false "you asked for".** Only say it when the supplier actually requested those terms, in its own term sheet or e-mail. In P01 and P18 the payment terms were just the supplier's standard, filled in from its contract. The code to change is `supplier_asks` in [strategy.py:280](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/strategy.py:280) and the sentence in [dual.py:772](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/dual.py:772).
2. **Stop the duplicate sentence.** The model writes its own "we gladly accept your requested terms" line on top of the one code already writes. It should be told code covers that point.
3. **Open at a price that fits our own argument.** For example, the current price × (1 + the weighted cost effect), instead of below today's price.

**The 25 % rule.** There was already a 25 % cap (`MAX_ANCHOR_CUT`), but it only covered the opening price. The option priced around a supplier's terms could still go down to the sheet floor. Without cost data that floor was 60 % of their price, which is how P18 got €4.39.
- A new `sheet_floor()` in [strategy.py](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/strategy.py) returns the higher of the supplier's cost floor and 75 % of their price.
- Both the dual agent ([dual.py:570](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/dual.py:570)) and the buyer agent ([buyer.py:336](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/buyer.py:336)) now use it. Every option, the cheaper extra option and the fallback counter are all held at or above it.
- In P18 the lowest possible offer is now €4.58 instead of €4.39. This alone may not fix P18: the agent can still send the same offer twice, which was the other half of that failure.

**One side effect.** If a supplier quotes more than about 33 % above our alternative, no allowed option can beat the alternative. The agent then sends no options and walks away. None of the 10 practice cases is like that: the alternative is always above the supplier's opening price. One existing test used that setup (a quote at 1.5× the alternative), so I changed it to 1.2×; what it checks is unchanged. I also added a regression test for the floor.

Should I re-run P18 (1 session) or all 10 cases (10 sessions) to measure this, and should I do fix 1 as well?

content.text:
P18 with the dual agent went from **0.000 to 0.252**: it closed at **€5.70** instead of €6.10. That's about €18.3k less total cost, from 295,173 to 276,889 EUR. This was one session; 403 practice sessions are left today.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Our first offer | €4.39 / €5.36 (28 % and 12 % under their price) | €5.22 / €5.33 / €5.40 (all within 14 % of their price) |
| Supplier's response | "far below any calculation", no move | Moved straight from €6.10 to €5.70 |
| Our next offer | The same two options again | New options (€5.28 / €5.48) |
| Deal | €6.10, 30 days, 12 months, no index clause | €5.70, 90 days, 24 months, alloy index clause |
| Score | 0.000 | **0.252** |

With a credible first offer, the supplier came down a full €0.40 in its first reply. It then held at €5.70 for two rounds, made that its final offer, and the agent accepted it.

There's still room left: the best possible deal (C best) is 222,651 EUR, so this deal is 54k EUR above it. Two things to look at next:
- **The index clause.** The deal ties 45 % of the price to the alloy index (AS-14404) with no deadband, so we carry the alloy risk. AGENTS.md already lists index-clause handling as an open problem for this case type.
- **One run is noisy.** Runs vary by about ±0.2 per case, so part of the jump could be chance. The change still isn't committed. Should I commit it to this branch?
